doc.title: Daryl Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2024

title: Jay Leonhart and the Anderson twins
summary: She talks about Jay Leonhart, a Blossom/Frishberg show, and working with Peter and Will Anderson on an Artie Shaw program and upcoming Mezzrow date.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Who was very busy in the studios. Yeah. Yeah. He’s going to be going to London, we’re going to do the Blossom/Frishberg show again. And he sings. So that adds another entertainment dimension. And now I have a twin act. Peter and Will Anderson, or Will and Peter Anderson went through the Juilliard School program. I met them because one of my friends was the director of a theater, 59 — East 59th . He discovered them busking in Central Park and hired them to play one night a week at the bar of the theater. And from that they, you know, they’re doing everything all over. They each play multi reeds, they’re smart, they’re adorable, they’re identical but you can tell them a little bit apart. And I did an Artie Shaw program with them, that’s how we got to know each other. And I sang, and we didn’t talk about that but I sang with Artie Shaw but not in the ‘30s, even though it may sound that way, in the ‘80s. But what’s fun is first of all they’re so quick. Even — they know a lot of the old songs. They’ve been playing regularly with Vince Giordano and the Nighthawks or David Ostwalt who is at Birdland playing the Louis Armstrong, so they know the whole tradition. But they can do all sorts of things. They read, and so I love just the three of us not even a bass, not even a drummer. And we’ll be at Mezzrow on the 18th , June 18. And we did something a month or so ago. And I’ll give them a song, I’ll indicate — sometimes I’ll write out a little line for them to play, once in a while. And sometimes we just wing it. And they — because they just have this, well © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

because they’re exceptional musicians, but I think they just have this twinny thing. They must. It is extraordinary, and the way they play together. And it sounds like I’m singing with an orchestra. And they’re cute. They’re so — they’re actually over 30 now, and they’re both fathers of now two children.
But I love doing that. And it’s so stimulating.
